Evidence: Exp 31 ends at gamma=0.106 despite HIL audit showing residuals were mostly harness issues and low/medium edge cases; a mandatory gamma gate would force false-nontermination under the exact failure mode we are trying to remove.

CONFIRM ChatGPT_F003

CONFIRM ChatGPT_F006

CHALLENGE CC2_F001 | Exp 30 does not evidence a state-only false positive
Evidence: your cited R5-R6 window still had 14 and 19 findings, not a lull by any practical stop rule. The stronger artifact signal is the opposite failure: gamma lagging qualitative closure in Exp 31.

CHALLENGE CC2_F004 | 4-primary default is not evidence-supported over 3+reserve
Evidence: the artifact gives efficiency by model, but no evidence that the 4th active primary produces enough unique high-value contribution to justify per-round cost. Under missing unique-severity data, simplest sufficient wins: 3 independent families plus escalation.

EXTEND ChatGPT_F008 | reserve escalation must be tied to canonical finding age and verdict split
Evidence: “unresolved after 1 full subsequent round” is directionally right, but the runner needs an exact trigger to avoid premature reserve activation on fresh findings.

FIX: The design should be locked to state-based termination, registry-centric transport, 3 primaries plus reserve, CC2 internal-only specialists, and bipartite schemas with runner-owned status.
FOLLOW: This package is coupled. If you keep gamma as a hard gate, the 8-round budget becomes internally inconsistent because a slow cumulative metric can force unnecessary extension even when OPEN target-code blockers are gone. If you keep model-emitted VERIFIED/STATUS, the registry topology cannot close findings reliably. If you use 3 primaries without exact reserve triggers, anti-deference will create unresolved contested findings and repeat BUDGET_EXHAUSTED under a different mechanism.

Definitive stance: lock the next experiment to a runner-owned canonical state model and remove gamma from the hard stop gate.
